# WO-609: Dry run pops a desktop notification; "5 minutes" for 400+ to-dos; drafted count wrong
Status: queued (in-house)
Vendor: claude
Agent: automation-engineer (Theo Park)
Owner contact: Morgan Reyes
Kind: engine
Severity: MEDIUM
Target release: 0.4
Source: owner real-data test, stage 1 (search only), qa-security 2026-11-11. Private results are kept outside the repo; this WO is PII-free by rule.

## Goal
`run --dry-run --headless` on the owner test folder (full registry, no removal mailbox) sent nothing (verified: no socket connect, no browser; see the qa note below), but:
1. It still fired a real desktop notification through `notify-send`: "Free My ID needs 5 minutes of your help - 414 things need you" (`engine/runner.py:1055-1069`). A practice run should not alert the person, or should say it was practice.
2. "5 minutes" is fixed text. With no mailbox, every email broker becomes a send-it-yourself letter: 366 letters + 47 assisted forms + 1 phone call. For the target user that is days, not minutes, and the number alone will scare them off.
3. `run/1` reported `drafted_emails: 0` while 366 DRAFT letters (dry_run=True) were created; the counter only counts `_queue_email` drafts (`runner.py:736`), not manual letters.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. Dry runs never call the notifier (or call it with a title that starts "Practice run:"); pick one and test it with a fake notifier.
2. Notification wording scales: small counts keep the friendly line; large counts say what the single next step is (e.g. "Set up a removal mailbox so Free My ID can send these for you") instead of a time estimate.
3. Drafted manual letters are counted (new `drafted_letters` or included in `drafted_emails`, documented); JSON doc change goes to the orchestrator as a CHANGE REQUEST for docs/CLI.md.
4. When no removal mailbox is set and more than N brokers need letters, the run summary leads with "Add a removal mailbox" (one line).
5. Tests with a fake notifier and a fake registry of 50 email brokers.
